title: Priority fingerprinting & contextual-temporal bucketing for per-tenant calibration suites
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: produce per-domain, per-tenant calibration suites for FP8/INT8 quantization that preserve end-user accuracy distributions while keeping pack size bounded for fast offline calibration and CI runs.

Background: Existing calibration packs are either oversized (expensive) or underrepresent temporal signal and tenant skew. We need a reproducible algorithm that prioritizes rare but high-impact prompt families, preserves contextual diversity (length, role mix, instruction vs. conversational), and respects recency so model regressions on fresh traffic are caught quickly.

Proposed approach (overview):
1) Priority fingerprinting: compute a compact fingerprint per prompt using a stable hashing of (domain, tenant_id, normalized_prompt_text, prompt_type). Attach a priority score that combines: frequency weight (inverse freq to upweight rare prompts), recent-activity multiplier (more weight for recent occurrences), and severity tag multiplier (high for prompts in closed-loop failure reports or customer flagging).
2) Contextual-temporal bucketing: bucket prompts along three orthogonal axes: domain (primary), token-length quantile (short/medium/long), and temporal window (0-7d, 8-30d, 31-90d, >90d). Within each bucket maintain a small reservoir sample with exponential decay retention so packs tilt toward recent data while retaining long-tail exemplars.
3) Per-tenant stratification: ensure each tenant with >= N requests contributes at least M exemplars to their domain pack to surface tenant-specific regressions. Tenants with < N aggregate into a shared "long-tail" cohort.
4) Pack assembly: deterministic seeding ensures repeatable packs for CI. Assembly procedure enforces constraints: total tokens <= calibrated_budget_tokens, max examples per tenant, and minimum bucket coverage.

Acceptance criteria:
- Calibration pack generation pipeline produces domain packs that:
  * Achieve equal or better calibration loss on holdout set compared to baseline stratified reservoir (target: <= 2% delta in mean calibration loss).
  * Surface at least 95% of recent high-severity failure types within top-1000 exemplars for a domain.
  * Pack generation completes within 30 minutes for a full tenant cohort (<= 10M requests window) on standard infra.
- End-to-end reproducibility: same seed + same input traffic snapshot -> identical pack.
- CI integration: pack used in quantization regression CI with known checkpoints (int8/fp8) and automated acceptance gating.

Implementation tasks:
- [ ] Design data schema for fingerprint and priority metadata (storage: parquet + indexed by domain).
- [ ] Implement priority scoring service (batch Spark job prototype).
- [ ] Build reservoir-with-decay sampler (Go service for streaming and library for offline pack generation).
- [ ] Pack assembler with rule-based constraints and deterministic RNG seeding.
- [ ] Unit + integration tests including reproducibility test harness.
- [ ] Benchmark compare vs current stratified-reservoir baseline (latency, pack quality, compute cost).
- [ ] Docs: Confluence design doc, usage guide for PM/Research, and automated note in Console for pack provenance.

Metrics to track:
- Calibration loss change (mean, 95th) on holdout vs baseline.
- Coverage of flagged failure types (recall@k).
- Pack generation runtime and memory.
- Token budget utilization and average exemplar length.
- Per-tenant exemplar distribution (to detect over/under-representation).

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Recency multiplier may overfit to transient noise -> Mitigation: add a minimum retention quota per bucket and monitor burstiness signals to cap weight.
- Risk: Priority score complexity adds operational cost -> Mitigation: provide a simple "fast mode" that uses only frequency+recency and a "full mode" with severity tags for nightly builds.
- Risk: Tenant privacy concerns when shipping per-tenant packs -> Mitigation: default to hashed tenant ids in pack artifacts; enable opt-out and aggregation for regulated customers.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype batch pipeline and run A/B compare on three domains (chat, search, docs) using last-90d traffic.
2) Iterate scoring weights with PM/IR feedback; produce 1st calibration packs for FP8 and INT8 and run quantization acceptance tests.
3) Integrate deterministic pack generation into quantization CI (canary lane) and monitor false-positive regression rate.
4) Gradual expansion to all domains and enable per-tenant quotas behind feature flag.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Priority+Fingerprinting+%26+Temporal+Bucketing
- Prototype notebook & benchmarks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/calibration-prototypes/tree/priority-fp
- CI PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci/pull/4123
- Pack visualizer (internal): https://console.redwood.ai/calibration/packs/view?domain=chat

Notes: aim to keep pack sizes small enough to be used in fast CI lanes (<= 10k examples / domain) while providing a separate large archival pack for deep QA runs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Generated packs must be reproducible given same seed and snapshot. 2) Pack quality within 2% mean calibration loss of baseline. 3) Pack generation runtime <= 30 minutes for 10M-requests window. 4) CI integration verified for int8 and fp8 workflows.
